verdictMeaning: A student picks a person and a place on the family's own land; the server says what ten acres there would be or refuses in a sentence; sent, the person walks out over their own land a tick at a time, stakes ten acres and walks back; the plot is stored, projected, drawn and in the story; on both maps; old saves validate.

browserProof.note: Same computer only. MAP=colonies PORT=8757 SEED=art-proof-4, five families, isolated data folder, the in-app browser. Not LAN acceptance.
observed: Hollis's work list offered 'Survey ten acres'; choosing it opened 'Where Hollis surveys' and put the person panel away.

The first tap, before the fix, read 'That runs into the water.' with no water drawn there; then 'That runs into Deadman Creek.' for a creek under five miles the map leaves off. Both fixed: only the class map's own water refuses.

After the fix the same tap read 'Ten acres of timber a quarter mile south-west of the house.' with a red dashed square; 'Survey it' drew Hollis walking out to a dashed square, and six seconds later the plot was a brown staked square, Hollis back in the yard, and the story read 'Hollis staked out ten acres of timber a quarter mile south-west of the house.'
Also found: choosing the house site exactly on the surveyor's mark returned 'Invalid travel' from the server (a journey of no length). Fixed and tested.
